title: Gazpacho
subtitle: Cold Andalusian tomato and vegetable soup
excerpt: Gazpacho is a cold raw tomato soup from Andalusia, southern Spain. It is made by blending very ripe tomatoes with cucumber, red pepper, garlic, sherry vinegar, and olive oil. Served ice-cold in summer with garnishes of chopped vegetables and croutons. The flavour depends entirely on the quality of the tomatoes.
sourceNotes: Gazpacho originates from Andalusia and has been documented since at least the 18th century. The word is of uncertain etymology; the dish may be related to pre-Roman peasant bread soups. The tomato was added after the Columbian exchange in the 16th century and became the defining ingredient.

recipe.batchNotes: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days. The flavour improves overnight.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best made the day before serving.

content.text: Gazpacho is only as good as its tomatoes. In summer, use the ripest, reddest tomatoes you can find. Out of season, the soup lacks sweetness and depth. Add a tablespoon of tomato puree to compensate. Strain through a fine sieve after blending for a smooth, restaurant-style gazpacho; or leave it chunky for the rustic version.

items.prepNote: day-old white bread, optional — thickens and enriches

content.text: Put all the vegetables and garlic into a blender. Add the breadcrumbs if using. Blend until smooth. This takes 2 to 3 minutes in a jug blender. With the motor running, pour in the olive oil in a thin stream to emulsify it.
Add the sherry vinegar and season with salt and white pepper. Blend again. Taste: the soup should be tangy, sweet from the tomato, and well-salted. Adjust with more vinegar or salt.

Pass through a fine sieve if you want a smooth soup. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours before serving. Serve ice-cold in chilled bowls with a trickle of olive oil. Offer garnishes alongside: diced cucumber, diced pepper, diced tomato, and croutons.

items.symptom: Soup tastes watery and lacks depth
items.cause: Tomatoes were not ripe enough, or the ratio of tomato to other vegetables was off
items.fix: Add a tablespoon of tomato puree and a pinch of caster sugar. Season more assertively with salt. Cold food needs more seasoning than hot food.
